justification: Changes when the daily DCP alarm reports an unfinished monitor run.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_monitor_runs: id 1 daily killed 2026-10-22 (finished_at NULL), ids 2 and 3 force runs finished 2026-10-23.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The query assumed a killed run eventually finishes; it never does, so run_unfinished was red for ever after finished runs 2 and 3.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Same query plus a NOT EXISTS on a later finished full run; ordered by id so tests do not depend on wall-clock times.

falsifiable_check.command: PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 python -m pytest -m database tests/test_verifyops_coverage_real_db.py -o addopts=
falsifiable_check.fails_when: a killed run stays red after a later full run finishes, or clears on a one-council or still-running run
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 4 hand mutants: 3 killed after adding the still-running case; the 4th (>= on id) is equivalent because the killed run itself never finished.

functions.name: measure
functions.input: an open database connection to production, read only
functions.output: every red key today, run_unfinished only while no later full run has finished
functions.if_none: a missing table raises and the caller exits 2

break_it.scenario: Run 1 killed by a deploy, then runs 2 and 3 finish
break_it.what_happens: silent noise: run_unfinished red for ever and frozen into the baseline
break_it.how: a later finished full run makes it old news

break_it.scenario: A one-council run finishes after a killed full run
break_it.what_happens: would hide that no full sweep completed

break_it.scenario: The next full run is still going
break_it.what_happens: would clear the alarm before anything finished
break_it.how: only a FINISHED later run supersedes

post_merge.manual_verify: python scripts/verifyops_coverage.py no longer prints *|*|run_unfinished while run 1 is the only unfinished run.
